accepts_alg_none.title: Accepts `alg:none` Tokens
accepts_alg_none.description: Whether the JWT verifier accepts tokens presented with alg=none (the unsigned-token mode in RFC 7519). An attacker can strip the signature and set alg=none to forge any claims. Secure = false (alg=none must be rejected at parse time, before signature dispatch).

access_token_ttl_minutes.title: Access Token TTL (Minutes)
access_token_ttl_minutes.description: Lifetime of an issued access token in minutes. Multi-hour or multi-day TTLs widen the window in which a stolen or otherwise compromised bearer remains valid; over 60 minutes is excessive for a bearer token without a working revocation channel.

audience_claim_validated.title: Audience (`aud`) Claim Validated
audience_claim_validated.description: Whether the verifier enforces the aud claim against this service's expected audience identifier, rejecting tokens minted for a different relying party. When false, a token issued for another audience can be replayed here.

cookie_httponly_flag.title: Auth Cookie `HttpOnly` Flag Set
cookie_httponly_flag.description: True when authentication-bearing cookies carry the HttpOnly attribute, preventing JavaScript (document.cookie) from reading them. Insecure default is false (cookie readable by injected script); secure value is true (cookie hidden from the DOM, only the browser attaches it to requests).

expiry_claim_validated.title: Expiry (`exp`/`nbf`) Claims Validated
expiry_claim_validated.description: Whether the verifier enforces the token's exp (and nbf) temporal claims, rejecting expired or not-yet-valid tokens. When false, expired tokens remain accepted, extending credential lifetime indefinitely.

identifier_entropy_bits.title: HMAC Signing Key Entropy (Bits)
identifier_entropy_bits.description: Measured/asserted entropy of the HMAC signing key in bits. Industry floor for symmetric secrets is 128 bits; values below this admit feasible offline cracking of a captured JWT signature.

issuer_claim_validated.title: Issuer (`iss`) Claim Validated
issuer_claim_validated.description: Whether the verifier enforces the iss claim against an allow-list of trusted issuers, rejecting tokens minted by untrusted authorities. When false, any issuer (including attacker-controlled) can mint accepted tokens.

jwt_signature_verified.title: JWT Signature Cryptographically Verified
jwt_signature_verified.description: Whether the application actually performs cryptographic signature verification on every JWT before trusting its claims — as opposed to decoding the payload without verifying (a common library-misuse pattern where decode() is called instead of verify()). Secure = true.

long_lived_token_in_browser_storage.title: Long-Lived Token in Browser Storage
long_lived_token_in_browser_storage.description: True when a multi-day token (e.g. refresh token, long-TTL access token) is persisted in browser-side storage where an XSS sink can drain it in one shot. Insecure default is true; secure value is false (long-lived material kept server-side or in HttpOnly cookies; only short-TTL access tokens transit the browser).

refresh_token_rotation_enabled.title: Refresh-Token Rotation Enabled
refresh_token_rotation_enabled.description: True when the token service issues a new refresh token on every use and invalidates the previous one (rotation-on-use). False means the same long-lived refresh token is accepted repeatedly, so a stolen token grants indefinite access.

rs256_to_hs256_confusion_possible.title: RS256-to-HS256 Key Confusion Possible
rs256_to_hs256_confusion_possible.description: Whether the verifier is vulnerable to the RS256->HS256 key-confusion attack: it does not validate that the key material's type matches the header's alg family, so an attacker can submit a token with alg=HS256 and have the verifier HMAC-verify it using the RSA public key as the shared secret. Includes the related kid-header-injection failure mode where the verifier follows an attacker-chosen kid to attacker-controlled key material. Secure = false (verifier enforces key-type/alg-family binding and constrains kid resolution to a trusted key set).

samesite_attribute_set.title: Cookie `SameSite` Attribute Present
samesite_attribute_set.description: Whether the session/bearer cookie is issued with a SameSite attribute. When false, the cookie has no SameSite policy, so the browser attaches it to cross-origin requests (including state-changing POSTs from attacker-controlled pages) — the standard CSRF preconditions.

samesite_mode.title: Cookie `SameSite` Mode
samesite_mode.description: The SameSite policy applied to the session cookie. 'Strict' and 'Lax' block (or substantially restrict) cross-site attachment of the cookie; 'None' opts the cookie back into being sent on cross-site requests and is functionally equivalent to the attribute being absent for CSRF purposes on state-changing endpoints.

secrets_masked_in_logs.title: Token Values Masked in Logs
secrets_masked_in_logs.description: Attestation that raw authentication token values are redacted, masked, or omitted from all logging and telemetry sinks — application logs, access logs, error reports, distributed-tracing spans, APM payloads, and third-party observability vendors. When false, log aggregators and tracing backends become a credential exfiltration surface.

sender_constrained.title: Sender-Constrained Tokens
sender_constrained.description: True when access tokens are cryptographically bound to the legitimate sender (e.g. DPoP RFC 9449, mTLS-bound tokens RFC 8705, or token binding) so a token captured from one host cannot be replayed from another. False when tokens are plain bearers usable by anyone who presents them, enabling XSS/extension/AiTM/log-scrape replay against the API.

server_side_revocation_supported.title: Server-Side Revocation Supported
server_side_revocation_supported.description: True when the token service maintains server-side state that can detect reuse of an already-rotated/revoked refresh token and revoke the affected token family. False means there is no reuse-detection or revocation path, so a replayed refresh token cannot be invalidated.

session_absolute_timeout_enforced.title: Absolute Session Timeout Enforced
session_absolute_timeout_enforced.description: Whether an absolute (non-sliding) session cap is enforced so that a refresh chain cannot extend access indefinitely. When false, long-lived sessions effectively become permanent regardless of access-token TTL.

session_id_regenerated_on_auth.title: Session ID Regenerated on Authentication
session_id_regenerated_on_auth.description: Whether the session identifier is rotated/regenerated when an anonymous session transitions to an authenticated session. When false, a pre-authentication session id remains valid post-login — the root cause of session fixation: an attacker who plants a known session id rides the victim's authenticated session once the victim logs in with that id.

signature_algorithm_pinned_server_side.title: Signature Algorithm Pinned Server-Side
signature_algorithm_pinned_server_side.description: Whether the verifier pins the expected JWT signature algorithm server-side (e.g. RS256) and rejects tokens whose alg header does not match — instead of trusting the token's alg header to select the verification routine. The root-cause control against algorithm-confusion attacks (alg=none, RS256->HS256 key confusion, kid header injection). Secure = true (algorithm is pinned and the header alg is ignored or strictly validated against the pinned value).

signing_key_csprng_generated.title: Signing Key CSPRNG-Generated
signing_key_csprng_generated.description: Operator-attested boolean indicating the HMAC signing key was generated by a cryptographically secure random number generator (CSPRNG) rather than chosen by a human, derived from a passphrase without a strong KDF, or sourced from a non-cryptographic RNG. False means the key's provenance does not guarantee unpredictability.

signing_key_high_entropy.title: Signing Key Has High Entropy
signing_key_high_entropy.description: Operator-attested boolean indicating the HMAC signing key (HS256/HS384/HS512 shared secret) has high entropy — sufficiently long and unguessable to resist offline brute-force and dictionary attack against a captured JWT. False means the key is weak/guessable (short, human-chosen, dictionary-derived, or known constant).

stored_in_js_accessible_storage.title: Token Stored in JS-Accessible Storage
stored_in_js_accessible_storage.description: True when authentication tokens are placed in JavaScript-accessible storage (localStorage or sessionStorage) on the browser, making them reachable by any injected script via DOM APIs. Insecure default is true (localStorage is the common bad pattern); secure value is false (tokens held in HttpOnly cookies or non-persistent in-memory only).

tls_only_transport.title: TLS-Only Token Transport
tls_only_transport.description: Attestation that the authentication token is transmitted exclusively over TLS-protected channels on every leg of its lifecycle (issuance, presentation, refresh, revocation). When false, the token traverses cleartext or mixed-mode transport at some point and can be sniffed off the wire or harvested from intermediate plaintext caches.

transmitted_in_url_or_query.title: Token Transmitted in URL or Query
transmitted_in_url_or_query.description: Attestation that the authentication token is conveyed in a URL component (query string, path, or fragment) rather than only in headers or request bodies. Tokens in URLs are captured by browser history, Referer headers sent to third parties, CDN/edge access logs, proxy logs, and analytics pipelines — making them harvestable by anyone with read access to those sinks even when the underlying TLS transport is clean.
